avatar.fallback: If the photo is missing or fails to load, the avatar shows the initials, or the icon if there's no name.
avatar.lead: A person’s photo, initials or icon, with an optional border and presence dot.
avatar.installNote: The avatar uses status-indicator for its dot, so add both.
avatar.variantsBody: variant picks the content. image, the default, shows the photo, and while it loads or if it fails falls back to initials from name, then to the user icon when there is no name. initials and icon show theirs even when a photo is passed. radius picks a rounded square or a circle, and border adds a ring inside the edge.
avatar.sizesBody: 32 for headers, cards and comments; 24 for dense tables and lists; 12 for inline mentions, where initials shrink to one letter at the 10px XXS size.
avatar.statusBody: status adds a Status Indicator at the end corner — bottom-right, or bottom-left in a right-to-left page. There is no dot unless you set one: it claims the person’s presence, so show it only when you know it.

a11y.name: name names the avatar in every variant: it is the photo’s alt, and hidden text behind the initials or icon, whose visible letters are not read out.
a11y.empty: Pass {emptyName} when a label beside the avatar already names the person, so it isn’t announced twice.
a11y.dot: The dot is read after the name — "Layla Haddad", then "Online", or "متصل" when the nearest lang is Arabic. Pass statusLabel to say more.
a11y.dir: Direction is inherited from dir, never a prop, so the dot always sits on the right corner for the page.

usage.photo: Photo, falling back to initials, then the user icon
usage.initials: Initials or the icon, whatever else is passed
usage.lazy: Long lists: defer photos below the fold, and give dense screens a sharper source
usage.circle: Circle with a border and a presence dot
usage.inline: Inline, beside a name that already says who it is

props.variant: What it shows: photo, initials or icon.
props.border: Adds a ring inside the edge.
props.name: Person’s name: the alt text and initials.
props.statusLabel: Dot’s accessible name, in the page language by default.

statusIndicator.onAvatar: The dot is meant to sit on an avatar, not on its own over a coloured surface.
statusIndicator.lead: A presence dot — online, away, busy or offline — with an accessible name, so colour never carries the status alone.
statusIndicator.variantsBody: status sets the colour: success for online, warning for away, destructive for busy and muted for offline.
statusIndicator.sizesBody: 8px with a 2px ring, or 4px with a 1px ring for the smallest avatar. The ring is the page background, drawn outside the dot, so it never changes its size.

a11y.colour: Colour alone can’t carry the status. Each dot carries hidden text: "Online", "Away", "Busy" or "Offline", or "متصل", "بعيد", "مشغول" or "غير متصل" when the nearest lang is Arabic. It follows a language change without a reload.
a11y.label: Pass label for more context, such as "Layla is online".
a11y.hidden: When the status is already written next to the dot, hide the dot with aria-hidden so it isn’t announced twice.
a11y.dir: The dot is a circle, so it has no direction. The parent decides where it sits; Avatar pins it to the end corner.

props.label: Accessible name, in the page language by default.

landing.introBody: Fasla provides a collection of reusable components that you can copy and paste into your apps. It's not a traditional component library — you own the code and can customize it however you want.
landing.getStartedBody: Install the CLI and add your first component.

radio.lead: A control for choosing exactly one option from a set.
radio.variantsBody: The layout variant wraps the control and its text in a bordered card, so the whole card becomes the target. Use it when the options carry a description; use the default when they are single words in a tight list.
radio.statesBody: Hover and focus are real CSS states rather than props — hover an option, or tab to it, to see them. Selection is carried by the dot alone; the card chrome does not change.

a11y.nativeInput: Renders a native {input}, so arrow-key navigation and form submission work without extra code.
a11y.group: Options sharing a name form one group, and only one can be selected.
a11y.describedBy: description is linked with aria-describedby; the control graphic is hidden from assistive technology.
a11y.direction: Direction is inherited from dir, never a prop, so the control can never disagree with the page.

installation.title: Installation
installation.lead: How to install and set up Fasla in your project.
installation.cliBody: The easiest way to add components is the CLI in the @smicolon/fasla-ui package. It takes two steps.
installation.cliInit: 1. Initialize Fasla, once per project. This writes components.json, which every add reads:
installation.cliPrevious: Set up with @smicolon/cli? If it was 0.4 or later, keep going with this command in the same project. Nothing needs re-running. If it was 0.3 or earlier, run npx @smicolon/fasla-ui@latest init once first. It repairs the project’s components.json, which the shadcn CLI can’t read until then, and moves the files those versions put in the wrong folder.
installation.cliDepsFallback: init also writes the cn helper and installs the two packages it imports with your project’s package manager. If that install fails, init prints the command to run, which is one of these:
installation.cliDepsTailwind3: On Tailwind 3, the command installs tailwind-merge@^2, as tailwind-merge 3 supports only Tailwind 4. init and add also replace a tailwind-merge that is, or could become, 3:
installation.cliAddInstalls: add then installs the packages the components import, with your project’s package manager, and skips any your project already has at a compatible version. If that install fails, add keeps the files it wrote and prints the command to run. To print the command instead of installing, add --no-install.
installation.themeBody: Components take every colour from your theme. init asks which of two layers you want and installs it. The shadcn CLI commands below install a layer too, or switch a project to the other one later. Both give you the base layer.
installation.themeSetupFirst: The shadcn commands need a project that is already set up, with a components.json. In a new project, run npx @smicolon/fasla-ui@latest init first, or npx shadcn@latest init. Run in a project without one, the shadcn CLI sets the project up itself, and the colours of the preset it picks replace Fasla’s.
installation.themeFasla: Starting from scratch: use Fasla’s colours. Fasla’s light and dark palette, its radius and the Geist font, on top of the base layer:
installation.themeNext14: On Next.js 14, set the project up with npx @smicolon/fasla-ui@latest init, not shadcn init: shadcn’s setup writes Tailwind 4 styles and loads Geist from next/font, and Next.js 14 has neither, so the build fails. Then leave out font-geist.json, as the Next.js 14 template already loads Geist:
installation.themeBrand: I have a brand: keep my colours. The base layer only: the tokens shadcn doesn’t have (success, warning, info and the soft tints), the type scale with Arabic line heights, the Arabic setting and the Cairo font. It changes no colour you already have:
installation.themeConfirm: The shadcn CLI asks Existing CSS variables and components will be overwritten. Continue? with No as the default, so type y. The base layer, theme-base, doesn’t change any colour your project already has.
installation.themeArabicFont: Arabic text is set in Cairo through the --font-arabic variable. To use another Arabic font, point --font-arabic at it.
installation.themeReplaces: Fasla’s base components replace shadcn’s components of the same name, such as button and badge, in components/ui. add asks before it replaces a file that isn’t Fasla’s. Blocks install to their own folder, components/blocks.
installation.manualBody: You can also copy components directly from the source code.
installation.manualTailwind3: On Tailwind 3, install tailwind-merge@^2 instead. tailwind-merge 3 supports only Tailwind 4, and on Tailwind 3 it drops classes it doesn’t know, such as outline:
installation.manualCn: 2. Add the cn utility to your project:
installation.manualCopy: 3. Copy each component from its file in the registry, such as https://fasla.smicolon.com/r/button.json for Button. https://fasla.smicolon.com/r/registry.json lists them all.
installation.manualCopyDetail: In each file, files holds the source in content and the path to save it at in target. dependencies lists the packages to install, and registryDependencies the other Fasla components it needs, which you copy the same way.
installation.inverseBody: A block on an inverted surface, such as the FAQ Dark Panel, paints it with three tokens: background-inverse, foreground-inverse and muted-foreground-inverse. Fasla’s theme sets them: the surface is dark in light mode and light in dark mode. They are the only way Fasla inverts a surface, so a block never forces a dark class on a section or borrows bg-foreground.
installation.inverseFallback: Adding such a block with either CLI also adds the tokens’ mapping. When your theme doesn’t set the tokens, each falls back to your page colours, swapped: foreground for the surface, background for its text. To set your own, define --background-inverse, --foreground-inverse and --muted-foreground-inverse for light and dark.
installation.inverseTailwind4: Adding the mapping by hand on Tailwind 4: these three lines go in your stylesheet’s @theme inline block.
installation.inverseTailwind3: On Tailwind 3, these go under theme.extend.colors in tailwind.config:

checkbox.lead: A control that allows the user to toggle between checked and not checked.
checkbox.variantsBody: Two types, as in Figma. default is the box and its label on their own. layout wraps them in a bordered card that is all one click target, and fills on hover.
checkbox.sizesBody: Three sizes. md is the default. The box is 16, 20 or 24px, and the label stays the same size.
checkbox.statesBody: Checked shows a tick, indeterminate shows a dash, and neither flips in right-to-left. Hover and focus are real CSS states rather than props. Hover a checkbox, or tab to it, to see them. Disabled dims the whole checkbox, label and description included.

a11y.nativeInput: Renders a native {input}, so Space toggles it and it submits with a form without extra code.
a11y.indeterminate: indeterminate sets the input's own property, so a screen reader announces the checkbox as mixed. A click clears it, as in the browser; keep the prop in step from your state.
a11y.describedBy: The checkbox is named by label alone, and description is linked with aria-describedby. The box is hidden from assistive technology.
a11y.direction: Direction is inherited from dir, never a prop. The box sits at the start of the line in both directions.

props.indeterminate: Shows a dash for a partly selected group.

switch.lead: A toggle control for switching between on and off states.
switch.variantsBody: Two styles, as in Figma. solid, the default, fills the track, with the primary colour when on. outline keeps the track on the page background, draws it with a 1px line, and fills the thumb instead.
switch.sizesBody: Three sizes. md is the default. The track is 32, 40 or 48px wide, and the label stays the same size.
switch.layoutBody: control-first, the default, puts the track before the label and lines the description up under the label. label-first puts the label at the start and the track at the end of a full-width row, for settings lists.
switch.statesBody: Focus is a real CSS state rather than a prop. Tab to a switch to see the ring. Disabled dims the whole switch, label and description included.

a11y.nativeInput: Renders a native {input}, so Space toggles it and it submits with a form without extra code.
a11y.describedBy: description is linked with aria-describedby; the track is hidden from assistive technology.
a11y.direction: Direction is inherited from dir, never a prop. The thumb always moves towards the end of the line when the switch turns on.

select.lead: Lets the reader choose one option from a list, or several. It has a label, helper text and a prefix icon, as Input does, shows several choices as badges or as text, and comes in four sizes and two corner shapes.
select.sizesBody: Four sizes: xs is 28px tall, sm 32px, md 36px and lg 40px, the same heights as Input. As on Input, only the height and the gap between the icon and the text change: the padding is 12px and the icons 16px at every size. The text is 14px, or 16px on screens narrower than 768px, so iOS does not zoom in.

radius.title: Radius
radius.body: radius="standard" rounds the corners by 8px, and radius="rounded" makes a pill. The focus ring follows the shape. The menu keeps its 8px corners either way.

select.statesBody: Focus is a real state, not a prop: tab to the field, or open it. The trigger draws the focus ring on keyboard focus and for as long as its menu is open. disabled dims the whole field to half opacity, its label and helper text included.

multiple.title: Multiple select
multiple.body: multiple lets the reader choose several options. The menu stays open while they choose, and a check marks each chosen option. The trigger shows the choices as badges, or as one line of text with display="text". Badges wrap onto more rows, and the field grows to hold them. Press a badge's × to remove it.
multiple.text: Shown as one line of text.

parts.title: Labels and icons
parts.body: The label, the note at the end of the label row, the helper text and the prefix icon work as they do on Input, so the two line up side by side in a form. Put the icon in startIcon; the field sizes it to match.
parts.name: Full name
parts.nameHelp: As it appears on your ID.
parts.branchHelp: We hold your order for 3 days.

menu.title: The menu
menu.body: The menu opens under the trigger, 4px below it and exactly as wide. Pointing at an option, or moving to it with the arrow keys, highlights it. A check at the end of the row marks the chosen option. Its space is always kept, so the text never moves. On a right-to-left page the check and the chevron swap ends.

long.title: Long options
long.body: An option longer than the menu is wide wraps onto more lines inside it. In the trigger, the chosen option stays on one line and ends in an ellipsis.
long.label: Pickup point

options.airport: King Khalid International Airport, Terminal 5, arrivals hall pickup counter
options.olaya: Al Olaya District, King Fahd Road, Building 14, ground floor

a11y.roles: Base UI gives the trigger, a button, the combobox role, and makes the menu a listbox of options. A hidden input submits the value with its form, under name.
a11y.keyboard: Enter, Space and the arrow keys open the menu. The arrow keys, Home and End move through the options, and typing a letter jumps to a matching one. Enter chooses, and Escape closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger.
a11y.label: label names the trigger, and the helper text is read with it. Without a label, pass aria-label. Pressing the label moves focus to the trigger without opening the menu.
a11y.badges: A badge's × is for the pointer, and screen readers skip it. From the keyboard, open the menu and choose the option again to remove it.
a11y.direction: Direction is inherited from dir, never a prop. The menu takes the page's direction, language and font from the trigger, though it renders at the end of body.

props.onOpenChange: Called when the menu opens or closes.

props.defaultOpen: Opens the menu on first render.
props.collisionAvoidance: How the menu avoids the window edge. By default it flips above the trigger when there is no room below; { side: "none" } keeps it below.

button.lead: Starts an action, or takes the reader somewhere else. Five types, three tones, four sizes and two radii, the same as the Figma set, with a loading state.
button.variantsBody: variant sets the type. default, secondary and destructive are filled. outline has a border on the inside, ghost fills only when you hover it, and soft lays a light tint over the card surface. link is text, underlined in every state.

tones.title: Tones
tones.body: tone picks the colour within a type: primary, secondary or destructive. Each variant has its own default, so variant="outline" on its own is the neutral outline, and adding tone="destructive" makes it the destructive one.

button.sizesBody: Four sizes: xs is 26px tall, sm 32px, md 36px and lg 40px. Icons are 16px at every size. For a button with only an icon, use the icon sizes on the Icon Button page.

radius.title: Radius
radius.body: radius="standard" rounds the corners by 8px, and radius="rounded" makes a pill. The focus ring follows the shape.

button.statesBody: Hover, pressed and keyboard focus are real CSS states, not props: hover a button, press it, or tab to it. Filled buttons fade when you hover and press them. Soft, outline and ghost buttons deepen their tint instead, and a link keeps its underline and fades. Disabled dims every variant to half opacity.

link.title: Link or ghost
link.body: Both are quiet, but they mean different things. Use ghost for an action on the same page, such as closing a panel, editing a row or opening a menu. Use link to go somewhere else, such as Forgot password?, Learn more or View all, and render it as a real link with asChild.

icons.title: With icons
icons.body: Put an icon before or after the label, as a child. The button sizes it to 16px and gives it the label's colour. Icons follow the reading direction; flip one that points, such as an arrow, with rtl:-scale-x-100.

button.loadingBody: loading shows a spinner, disables the button and announces loadingLabel to screen readers. With asChild the child is only marked busy (aria-busy) and disabled, so show your own progress inside it.

a11y.nativeButton: Renders a native button, so Enter and Space press it. Set type="submit" or type="button" as the form needs.
a11y.focus: Keyboard focus draws a 2px ring, 2px outside the button, in the ring colour.
a11y.asChild: With asChild, the button styles its only child, such as a link. A disabled child gets aria-disabled instead of disabled.
a11y.loading: While it is loading, the button is disabled and announces loadingLabel as a status.
a11y.direction: Direction is inherited from dir, never a prop. Icons and label swap ends in right-to-left.

button.propsNote: Kept for shadcn compatibility: secondary and destructive still work as variant values (Solid in those tones), and default and icon as size values (the same as md and icon-md).

props.variant: The type: filled, outline, ghost, soft or link.
props.tone: The colour within the type. Each variant has its own default.
props.size: The height. The icon sizes are for icon buttons.
props.radius: The corners: slightly rounded, or a pill.
props.loading: Shows a spinner and disables the button.
props.asChild: Styles its only child, such as a link, instead of rendering a button.
props.onClick: Called when the button is pressed.

iconButton.lead: A square button with one icon and no label, for toolbars and dense rows. It is the Button component at an icon size, so it has the same variants, tones, states and radius.
iconButton.installNote: Icon Button is part of the button item, so installing Button installs it.
iconButton.variantsBody: Four variants, as in Figma's Icon Button: default, soft, outline and ghost, each in the three tones. There is no link icon button: an icon on its own does not read as a link.
iconButton.sizesBody: Four square sizes: icon-xs is 26px, icon-sm 32px, icon-md 36px and icon-lg 40px. The icon is 16px at every size.
iconButton.statesBody: Hover, pressed and keyboard focus are real CSS states, as on Button. Filled icon buttons fade; soft, outline and ghost ones deepen their tint. Disabled dims every variant to half opacity.

name.title: Accessible name
name.body: An icon has no text a screen reader can read, so every icon button needs a name: an aria-label, or text inside it that you hide visually. In development, the button warns in the console when it has none. To show the name on hover too, wrap the button in a tooltip.

a11y.label: Give every icon button an aria-label. The button warns in development when it has no name.
a11y.icon: The icon is decorative. Hide it from assistive technology with aria-hidden if your icon library does not.
a11y.focus: Keyboard focus draws a 2px ring, 2px outside the button, in the ring colour.
a11y.target: At icon-xs the button is 26px square. WCAG 2.5.8 asks for at least 24px, so every size passes.

iconButton.propsNote: Kept for shadcn compatibility: secondary and destructive still work as variant values (Solid in those tones), and icon as a size value (the same as icon-md).

props.size: The icon sizes: square, with one 16px icon.
props.ariaLabel: The name a screen reader reads. Required unless the button has visually hidden text.
props.variant: The type: filled, outline, ghost or soft.
props.tone: The colour within the type. Each variant has its own default.
props.radius: The corners: slightly rounded, or a circle.
props.loading: Replaces the icon with a spinner and disables the button.
props.asChild: Styles its only child, such as a link, instead of rendering a button.
props.onClick: Called when the button is pressed.

skeleton.lead: Placeholders that hold the shape of content while it loads, so the page doesn't jump when it arrives.
skeleton.buildBody: For layouts the three ready-made skeletons don't cover, compose your own from single blocks.
skeleton.basicBody: A single block, sized with className. It replaces shadcn's Skeleton with no other changes.
skeleton.variantsBody: variant sets the shape of a block: a bar with a 4px radius, a circle, or square corners.
skeleton.textBody: SkeletonText draws full-width lines, 16px tall and 8px apart. It shows 2 lines unless you set lines.
skeleton.avatarBody: SkeletonAvatar is a 48px circle. Pass another size in className to match a smaller or larger avatar.
skeleton.listItemBody: SkeletonListItem puts an avatar at the start of the line and text lines beside it, 16px apart. Use it for lists, comments and profile rows.
skeleton.cardBody: SkeletonCard is a 122px media block above 2 text lines. It has no border or background of its own, so place it inside a Card when the real content has one.

a11y.decorative: Every block is aria-hidden, so screen readers skip the placeholders.
a11y.busy: Mark the region that is loading with aria-busy="true", and set it to false when the content arrives.
a11y.motion: The pulse stops when the user turns on prefers-reduced-motion. Set animate to false to turn it off everywhere.
a11y.direction: Direction is inherited from dir, never a prop. The avatar always sits at the start of the line.

props.variant: The shape of a single block: a rounded bar, a circle or a rectangle.
props.animate: Pulses while loading. The pulse always stops under reduced motion.
props.lines: Number of text lines in SkeletonText, SkeletonListItem and SkeletonCard.
props.className: Sets the size, such as h-4 w-48.

usage.loading: Mark the region that is loading

tabs.lead: Tabs switch between related views in the same place and show one panel at a time. The same component is sometimes called Pills.
tabs.installNote: Tabs is built on Base UI, so it needs the @base-ui/react package. add installs it with the component, and so does the shadcn CLI.
tabs.variantsBody: Three styles, set on TabsList so a group never mixes them. boxed, the default, sets the tabs in a muted track and raises the active tab into a pill on it; it suits toolbars and inline view switches. bordered underlines the active tab, for content navigation and dense layouts. lifted raises the active tab out of a baseline like a file folder, for page-level sections.
tabs.sizesBody: Three sizes, also set on TabsList so every tab in a group matches. md is the default. Tabs are 28, 30 or 32px tall, and lg uses 16px text with 20px icons. The boxed track adds 4px around them.
tabs.statesBody: The active tab follows value. Hover and focus are real CSS states rather than props, so tab into a group to see the focus ring. A disabled tab is greyed out, and you cannot select it.

panels.account: Make changes to your account here.
panels.billing: Review your plan and invoices here.

disabled.label: Orders
disabled.currentText: You have two orders out for delivery.

a11y.roles: Renders the tablist, tab and tabpanel roles. Each tab points to its panel with aria-controls while that panel is shown, and the panel takes its name from its tab through aria-labelledby.
a11y.keyboard: Tab enters the group on the active tab. The arrow keys move to the previous or next tab and select it, wrapping at the ends. To select with Enter or Space instead, set activateOnFocus to false. Home and End jump to the first and last tab. The arrow keys also reach a disabled tab, so a screen reader announces it, but it cannot be selected.
a11y.label: Give TabsList an aria-label that names the group.
a11y.icons: An icon before the label is decorative, so mark it aria-hidden and let the label name the tab.
a11y.direction: Direction is inherited from dir, never a prop. In right-to-left pages the arrow keys follow the reading order, so the left arrow moves to the next tab.

props.defaultValue: Tab active at first. Without it or value, the first enabled tab is active.
props.onValueChange: Called when the active tab changes. Call eventDetails.cancel() to refuse the change.
props.variant: How the active tab is shown. Set on TabsList.
props.size: Size of every tab in the group. Set on TabsList.
props.activateOnFocus: Whether the arrow keys also select the tab they move to. Set on TabsList.
props.trigger: A tab button; its value names its panel, and disabled turns it off.

tooltip.lead: A short hint that appears while the pointer rests on an element or keyboard focus reaches it. Use it to name an icon button or add one line of context, and keep anything the reader must see on the page itself.
tooltip.installNote: Tooltip is built on Base UI, so it needs the @base-ui/react package, and its avatar slot uses avatar. add installs both with the component, and so does the shadcn CLI.
tooltip.previewHint: Hover over the button, or move to it with Tab.
tooltip.variantsBody: Six styles, set with variant. primary, the default, suits everyday labels, and secondary is a quieter neutral. info, success, warning and destructive carry the status colours: pick the one that matches what the message means, and make the words clear on their own. radius chooses between 8px corners for standard and 16px for rounded, which reads as a pill on a single line.

placement.title: Placement
placement.body: side picks the side of the trigger the tooltip sits on, and the arrow points back at it. top, bottom, left and right are fixed sides of the screen, so left stays put on a right-to-left page. inline-start and inline-end mean the start and end of the line, so they swap sides in Arabic. When there is no room, the tooltip flips to the opposite side. Set arrow to false to drop the arrow.

content.title: Content
content.body: The text you put inside is the title. description adds a second, less prominent line. icon puts a 16px glyph before the text, in the text colour, and avatar puts a round 12px avatar in the same place, to show who the hint is about. The text wraps at 296px, so a tooltip is at most 320px wide, or 340px with an icon.

sample.title: Copy link

sample.longTitle: Changes you make here apply to every member of this workspace, including people who join later.
sample.longDescription: Members can still override this setting for their own account from their profile page.

a11y.hint: A tooltip is a visual hint: Base UI gives it no role and does not link it to the trigger. Give the trigger its own accessible name, as visible text or an aria-label, and keep essential information out of the tooltip.
a11y.keyboard: It opens as soon as the pointer rests on the trigger or keyboard focus reaches it, and closes when either leaves or when you press Escape.
a11y.interactive: Keep links and buttons out of a tooltip. It closes as focus moves, so nobody can reach them.
a11y.colour: The status styles add colour, not meaning. Say what kind of message it is in the words, or add an icon that does.
a11y.direction: The tooltip takes its direction, language and font from the trigger, even though it renders at the end of body. Direction is never a prop.

usage.logical: At the end of the line

props.open: Shows or hides the tooltip, when controlled.
props.onOpenChange: Called when the tooltip opens or closes.
props.render: Replaces the default button with your element, such as a link or a Button.
props.radius: 8px corners, or 16px: a pill on one line.
props.side: Side of the trigger it sits on. The inline-* sides follow the reading direction.
props.align: Where along that side it lines up with the trigger.
props.sideOffset: Distance from the trigger to the tooltip, in px.
props.description: A second line under the title.
props.avatar: Props for an Avatar before the text, always at size 12.
props.container: The element the tooltip renders into. Defaults to body.
props.delay: How long to wait before opening, in milliseconds.
props.onOpenChangeComplete: Called once the tooltip has finished opening or closing.
props.disableHoverablePopup: Closes the tooltip as soon as the pointer leaves the trigger, even onto the tooltip.
props.trackCursorAxis: Makes the tooltip follow the pointer along one axis, or both.
props.actionsRef: A ref to close or unmount the tooltip from your own code.
props.handle: Links the tooltip to triggers rendered elsewhere. Create it with Tooltip.createHandle() from @base-ui/react/tooltip.
props.triggerId: Which of several triggers the tooltip belongs to, when open is controlled.
props.defaultTriggerId: Which trigger the tooltip belongs to on first render, with defaultOpen.
props.closeDelay: How long to wait before closing, in milliseconds.
props.closeOnClick: Closes the tooltip when the trigger is pressed.
props.triggerDisabled: Stops this trigger from opening the tooltip.
props.triggerHandle: The handle of a tooltip rendered elsewhere that this trigger opens.
props.payload: Data passed to the tooltip when this trigger opens it.
props.alignOffset: Moves the tooltip along its side, in px.
props.collisionAvoidance: How the tooltip avoids the window edge. { side: "none", align: "none" } keeps it in place.

progress.lead: A bar that shows how much of a task is done, from 0 to 100%. It comes in three sizes, can show the percentage before the bar, and fills from the start of the line, so it follows the page's reading direction.
progress.showPercentageBody: With showPercentage set to false, the bar shows no number, so give it an aria-label that says what it tracks. Screen readers announce that name with the value. See the example in Storybook.

props.value: How much is done, from 0 to 100. Values outside the range are clamped.
props.showPercentage: Shows the percentage before the bar.
props.ariaLabel: Names the progress bar for screen readers.
props.getAriaValueText: Returns the text screen readers hear for the value.
props.locale: Locale used to format the percentage.

pagination.lead: A row of page links for moving through a long list or a set of results. The page links, Previous and Next are all Buttons, in three variants, two shapes and four sizes, the same as the Figma set.
pagination.installNote: Pagination is built on Button, so adding it adds button too.
pagination.variantsBody: variant picks the Button type of each part. default has ghost page links and a solid current page. solid has soft page links and a solid current page. outlined has outline page links, a soft current page, and outline Previous and Next. In the other two, Previous and Next are ghost.
pagination.sizesBody: The four Button sizes: xs is 26px tall, sm 32px, md 36px and lg 40px. A page link is a square of that height, and its number is 14px at every size. A number too wide for its square, such as 100 at xs, widens it.

shape.title: Shape
shape.body: shape="square" gives every part the Button's standard 8px corners, and shape="rounded" its full radius: circles for the page links, pills for Previous and Next. The focus ring follows the shape.

steps.title: Previous and Next
steps.body: PaginationPrevious and PaginationNext show a label and a chevron. The label follows the page's language, Previous and Next or السابق and التالي; pass text to change it. With iconOnly they show the chevron alone in a square, and keep the label for screen readers. Disable Previous on the first page and Next on the last with disabled.

long.title: Long ranges
long.body: Show the first and last pages, the current page with one on each side, and put PaginationEllipsis where pages are left out: 1 … 5 6 7 … 20. The ellipsis is a square the size of a page link, but not a link, and screen readers hear “More pages”. Icon-only Previous and Next keep a long row short. On a phone, show fewer pages around the current one, as this example does.

a11y.landmark: Pagination is a nav landmark. Name it in the page's language with aria-label, as the examples here do; otherwise it is called Pagination. Give each one on a page its own name.
a11y.current: The current page carries aria-current="page", so screen readers announce it as the current page.
a11y.steps: Previous and Next are named by their label, which stays readable when iconOnly hides it. The chevrons are hidden from assistive technology.
a11y.ellipsis: The ellipsis takes no focus. Its glyph is hidden, and screen readers hear “More pages”, or “مزيد من الصفحات” when the nearest lang is Arabic.
a11y.disabled: A disabled link carries aria-disabled, leaves the tab order and ignores clicks. It stays a link, so screen readers still find it.
a11y.focus: Every part is a Button, so keyboard focus draws the Button's 2px ring, 2px outside the link.
a11y.direction: Direction follows the page's dir; there is no prop. Right to left, the row starts on the right with Previous, and each chevron turns to point outward. Page numbers stay in Western digits.

pagination.variant: The Button type of each part: ghost, soft or outline page links.
pagination.shape: The corners of every part: the Button's standard radius, or its full radius.
pagination.size: The height of every part, from 26px to 40px.
pagination.ariaLabel: The landmark's name for screen readers, in the page's language.
pagination.className: Extra classes for the nav element, a centred row by default.

content.className: Extra classes for the ul element. It wraps onto a second row rather than overflow.

item.children: One page link, Previous, Next or the ellipsis.

link.href: Where the link goes. The link takes every other attribute of an a element too.
link.isActive: Marks the current page: the current-page look and aria-current="page".
link.disabled: Dims the link, takes it out of the tab order and ignores clicks.
link.asChild: Makes its only child the link, with these styles: Next.js's Link, say, or a button when paging changes state rather than the URL.
link.children: The page number, in Western digits on Arabic pages too.

step.text: The label. Previous or Next by default, in the page's language.
step.iconOnly: Shows the chevron alone, in a square. The label stays for screen readers.
step.disabled: Dims the link, takes it out of the tab order and ignores clicks.
step.asChild: Makes its only child the link, and puts the label and chevron inside it.

ellipsis.className: Extra classes for the ellipsis. Its screen-reader text is built in.

accordion.lead: Accordion stacks headings that each show or hide a section of content. Use it for questions and answers, settings groups and other content people scan before they read it in full.
accordion.installNote: Accordion is built on Base UI, so it needs the @base-ui/react package. add installs it with the component, and so does the shadcn CLI.
accordion.previewHint: Select a question, or move to it with Tab and press Enter or Space.
accordion.variantsBody: Four styles, set with variant on Accordion so every item in a group matches. default divides the items with a line and suits FAQ pages. split sets each item on its own card with a shadow, and outline draws a border round each one. Both leave 8px between items, for an accordion that sits beside other cards. table draws one box round the whole group, for structured details.

indicator.title: Indicator
indicator.body: indicator sets the mark at the end of each heading. chevron, the default, points down and turns to point up while the item is open. plus shows a plus that becomes a minus, which makes the action explicit. The mark sits at the end of the line, so on a right-to-left page it moves to the other side on its own.

composition.title: Avatars, icons and nested accordions
composition.body: Put an Avatar or a 16px icon before the title, inside AccordionTrigger, and the row leaves 12px between them. Hover underlines the title only. Hide the avatar or icon from screen readers with aria-hidden, because the title already names the row. To line the content up under the title, indent it with a class such as ps-11 on AccordionContent. For a second level, put another Accordion inside AccordionContent, and keep it for content that really has parents and children.

props.variant: The look of every item in the group.
props.indicator: The mark at the end of each heading.
props.multiple: Lets more than one item stay open at a time.
props.defaultValue: The items open on first render, by their value.
props.value: The open items, when you control them.
props.onValueChange: Called with the open items whenever one opens or closes.
props.hiddenUntilFound: Lets the browser's find in page search closed items and open the one it finds.
props.item: One item. Its value is what value and defaultValue list.
props.trigger: The heading: the title, with an optional avatar or icon before it. The indicator is added for you.
props.content: The section that opens under the heading.
props.className: Extra classes. On AccordionContent they go on the inner box, which holds the padding.

badge.lead: A compact inline label for status, category or metadata, with an optional icon, avatar and close button.
badge.variantsBody: variant sets the visual weight and tone the meaning. Solid is the loudest; Soft lays a tint over the card surface, so it reads the same wherever it sits; Outline is the quietest.
badge.radiusBody: {radiusStandard} swaps the pill for the design system’s small radius.
badge.sizesBody: Heights are minimums: 20, 22 and 26px in English. Arabic’s taller line grows them to 24, 24 and 28px rather than squeezing the text.
badge.statesBody: Pass onClose and the badge gets a real close button. Tab to one to see the focus ring, which wraps the whole badge 2px out.

a11y.span: The badge is a plain {span}. Only the close button is interactive, and it is a native {button}.
a11y.closeName: The close button is named after the label, "Remove Cairo", or "إزالة القاهرة" when the nearest lang is Arabic. It follows a language change without a reload. Pass closeLabel for more context, such as "Remove filter: Cairo".
a11y.icon: The icon is decorative and hidden from assistive technology. The avatar is not: give the Avatar a name, or {emptyName} when the label already names the person.
a11y.tone: Don’t rely on tone alone to carry meaning — the label should say it.
a11y.dir: Direction is inherited from dir, never a prop, so the badge can never disagree with the page.

usage.iconAvatar: Icon and avatar — the badge sizes and colours them
usage.photoNote: The photo from your own data. Without one, the avatar shows the user icon.

props.onClose: Adds a close button; called when pressed.
props.closeLabel: Close button’s accessible name, in the page language by default.

formSection.partsNote: The table covers the props of FormSection, FormField and FormActions.

props.title: Section title.
props.description: Text below the title or label.
props.divider: Shows a divider at the bottom.
props.label: Field label.
props.htmlFor: Connects the label to its input.
props.sticky: Sticks the actions to the bottom.

dataTable.paginationBody: Page through rows with Pagination, placed under the table. Here its links are buttons, because paging changes the rows shown rather than the URL.

props.columns: Column definitions; each align is start, center or end of the reading direction.
props.emptyState: Shown when there are no rows.
props.onRowClick: Called when a row is clicked.
props.stickyHeader: Keeps the header visible on scroll.

navbar.lead: A responsive navigation bar with mobile menu support.

props.sticky: Sticks to the top on scroll.
props.content: A section aligned to the start, centre or end.

props.title: Label above the value.
props.trend: Change, with an up or down arrow.
props.grid: Lays the cards out in 2, 3 or 4 columns.

shimmerButton.lead: A button with a sheen that sweeps across it, for the one call to action that matters most on the page.
shimmerButton.coloursBody: background takes any CSS colour or gradient, and shimmerColor sets the sheen. CSS variables such as var(--chart-2) follow light and dark mode.

a11y.button: It is a native {button}, so it takes its usual attributes, such as onClick, disabled and type, and shows a focus ring on Tab.
a11y.motion: With prefers-reduced-motion set, the sheen is not drawn, and the button looks the same without it.
a11y.dir: The sheen sweeps in the reading direction: left to right in English, right to left in Arabic.
a11y.contrast: The label uses --primary-foreground. With a custom background, check that the label still has enough contrast.

props.shimmerSize: Width of the sheen, as a length or a percentage of the button.
props.native: Native button attributes, such as onClick and disabled.

animatedGradient.lead: A background of slow-moving colour blobs, for hero sections and cards.

content.title: The autumn edit is here
content.body: New pieces in linen, wool and leather, in store now.

animatedGradient.coloursBody: colors takes up to four colours, one per blob. CSS variables such as var(--chart-1) follow light and dark mode.

a11y.decorative: The gradient is decoration: it has no role, and nothing in it for assistive tech to read.
a11y.motion: With prefers-reduced-motion set, the blobs stay still.
a11y.contrast: Text on the gradient must keep enough contrast wherever the blobs move.

props.children: Content on top of the gradient.
props.colors: Colours of the blobs, one each.
props.speed: Seconds for one cycle; higher is slower.
props.gradientText: Text filled with a moving gradient.

textReveal.lead: Reveals text a character at a time as it scrolls into view. Arabic reveals a word at a time, so its letters stay joined.
textReveal.wordBody: WordReveal reveals a word at a time, with a soft blur. It suits longer lines, in any language.
textReveal.word: Free delivery on every order in Riyadh this week.
textReveal.joinedBody: Arabic letters join to their neighbours, and a separate element for each letter would break those joins. So when the text contains Arabic, the effect reveals it a word at a time. Latin text keeps the character reveal.

a11y.whole: Assistive tech reads the whole text once; the animated pieces are hidden from it.
a11y.motion: With prefers-reduced-motion set, the text appears at once.
a11y.view: With triggerOnView, the effect waits until half the text is on screen, then plays once.

props.delay: Seconds between one piece and the next.
props.duration: Seconds each piece takes to appear.
props.triggerOnView: Waits until the text is on screen.
props.wordReveal: The same, a word at a time; delay defaults to 0.1 and duration to 0.4.

card.title: Autumn sale ends tonight
card.body: Up to 30% off linen and wool.

borderBeam.glowBody: To highlight a card without motion, use GlowingBorder instead of the beam. It draws a still coloured border with a soft glow close to it.

a11y.decorative: The beam is decoration and ignores the pointer; the content inside works as usual.
a11y.motion: With prefers-reduced-motion set, the beam is replaced by a still border at half strength.

props.borderWidth: Width of the beam in pixels.
props.colorFrom: Colour at the head of the beam.
props.glowingBorder: A still coloured border with a tight glow.

spotlight.lead: A soft light that follows the pointer across a section.

panel.title: Meet the autumn edit
panel.body: Move your pointer across this panel.

spotlight.cardBody: SpotlightCard is a card that lights up under the pointer while you hover over it.

card.title: Free delivery
card.body: On every order in Riyadh this week.

a11y.pointer: The light follows a mouse or trackpad only. Keyboard and touch users never see it, so put nothing in it that they need.
a11y.motion: With prefers-reduced-motion set, there is no light at all.

props.children: Content on top of the light.
props.size: Diameter of the light in pixels.
props.blur: Softness of the edge in pixels.
props.spotlightCard: A card that lights up under the pointer.

typewriterText.lead: Types text out a character at a time, with a blinking cursor.
typewriterText.preview: Your order is on its way.
typewriterText.wordsBody: TypewriterWords types a word, deletes it and moves on to the next.

a11y.cursor: The cursor is hidden from assistive tech.
a11y.motion: With prefers-reduced-motion set, the full text appears at once, with no cursor.
a11y.reading: A screen reader reads the text as it stands when it gets there, which may be half typed. Give the same message elsewhere on the page.

props.loop: Types the text again after a pause.
props.onComplete: Called when the text is fully typed.
props.typewriterWords: Types, deletes and cycles through a list of words.

glowCard.containerBody: GlowContainer draws a glow that slides round the border, in the reading direction. It moves on its own and doesn’t react to the pointer.
glowCard.container: Members get early access to the autumn edit.

a11y.decorative: The glow is decoration; the card's content works as usual.
a11y.hover: With hoverOnly, keyboard and touch users never see the glow, so put nothing in it that they need.
a11y.motion: With prefers-reduced-motion set, GlowCard shows no glow and the border of GlowContainer stays still.

props.glowIntensity: Blur of the glow in pixels.
props.followMouse: Moves the glow with the pointer.
props.hoverOnly: Shows the glow only on hover.
props.glowContainer: A container with a glow that slides round its border.

blocksIntro.title: Introduction
blocksIntro.lead: Blocks are whole page sections, built from Fasla’s components and ready to drop into a page.
blocksIntro.whatBody: A block is one file that composes Fasla components, such as Accordion, Tabs and Button, into a section of a page. It takes every colour from your theme tokens. Once it is in your project, the code is yours to change.
blocksIntro.whatResponsive: It is responsive: each block is designed at desktop, tablet and mobile widths, and changes layout at the md and lg breakpoints.
blocksIntro.whatDirection: It follows the page’s direction. Every side is a logical one, so the same code lays out left to right in English and right to left in Arabic.
blocksIntro.whatContent: Its content comes from props. Each block ships with English and Arabic copy; locale picks which, and any prop you pass replaces it.
blocksIntro.imagesBody: Blocks don’t include images. A block with a photo shows a placeholder, and one with people shows their initials, until you pass your own: image takes a src and an alt, and each person takes a src.
blocksIntro.inverseBody: A few blocks sit on an inverted surface: dark in light mode, light in dark mode. They are painted with the inverse tokens, so they never force a dark class on a section. Installing one with npx @smicolon/fasla-ui@latest add or npx shadcn@latest add also adds the tokens’ mapping to your stylesheet.
blocksIntro.inverseMore: Installing one by hand takes three lines of CSS: see <link>Installation</link>.

faqBlocks.intro: Each one installs on its own. Preview it at desktop, tablet or mobile width, in either direction. New to blocks? Start with the <link>introduction</link>.

blocksInstall.lead: Set your project up once, then add a block with one command.
blocksInstall.initBody: Run init once per project, before the first block. It writes components.json, which every add reads, adds the cn helper the blocks import, and installs the theme.
blocksInstall.initMore: The theme layers and setting up a project by hand: see <link>Installation</link> in the Components section.
blocksInstall.addBody: add writes the block to components/blocks/. It also installs the components the block uses, such as accordion or tabs, and the packages they import. You don’t add them one by one.

footer.line: Built in Germany by Smicolon GmbH · MIT core
footer.credits: Fasla is an Arabic-first React component library. Its components, blocks and templates are designed right-to-left from the start, not mirrored as an afterthought, and come with paired Cairo and Geist type, shared Tailwind tokens and a matching Figma library. You own the source, and you ship Arabic and English from one codebase.

type.title: Cairo is a 1:1 twin of Geist.
type.lede: Every step of the English ramp has an Arabic twin at the same size and weight. Only the line-height grows, so Arabic dots and ascenders have room to breathe.
type.note: Each row shares one baseline. Flip the page and the columns trade places; the type does not change.

items.a: Fasla (فاصلة) is a bilingual design system and React component library by Smicolon. Every component ships in English and Arabic, left-to-right and right-to-left, light and dark.

items.q: How is it different from shadcn/ui?
items.a: Fasla is built on shadcn/ui primitives and keeps its copy-the-source model. The difference is direction: RTL and the Arabic type ramp are part of every component from the first commit.

items.q: Do I design my Arabic screens separately?
items.a: No. An Arabic screen uses the same components as the English one with one property changed, Direction = RTL. Layout, icons and spacing mirror on their own.

Yes. The core is MIT licensed and free forever, for personal and commercial work. Pro is $149 and Team is $399, both one-time payments with lifetime access to the premium blocks, templates and the Figma file. <link>See the plans</link>.

items.q: How do I add it to my project?
items.a: Run init once, then add components one by one. The CLI copies each component's source into your repo, so you edit it like any file you wrote.
Yes. The Figma file is the source of truth and uses the same tokens as the code, so a designer's choice and a developer's build stay one decision.

items.q: Which fonts and numerals does it use?
items.a: Geist for English and Cairo for Arabic, on twin type ramps. Arabic copy uses Western numerals, and brand and technical terms stay in Latin script.

items.q: Can AI agents use the components?
items.a: That's where it's heading. Each component is documented with clear content rules, so an agent can pick the right one and fill it without breaking the layout.
